reviewer: Kimi independent actual visual comparison of the exact 65x67 source PNG, enlarged existing source-page 12 and targeted source-note crop, complete unchanged external-02 2048x2048 raw RGBA and native note/right-edge crop, full repair-agent white/cyan/alpha sheet and evidence, and unchanged naiwa.png; checked the corrected beard boundary, rectangular spectacles, suit/green tie, pose, collar, backing, restored row count versus prohibited dot replacement, and right-edge tab.

remaining_reasons: External-02 restores two rows and adds a dark right-edge tab, but BOTH rows are still regular circular dots rather than the source's irregular compact gray-mark groups. The requirement was not merely to restore row count and explicitly not to substitute dots. Replace the two dot rows with the original source-scale indistinct gray-mark shapes, footprint and spacing; do not invent letters, circular glyphs or extra marks.
entries.positive_observation: The corrected beard boundary is retained: the pale moustache and white beard remain around the lower mouth and chin while the upper cheeks between the spectacle rims and beard are smooth yellow without a broad cheek/temple beard. Brown side-parted hair, narrow sideburns, separate dark brows and dark rectangular spectacles remain, with one stern closed mouth. The slight left three-quarter pose, dark charcoal-brown suit, light pointed collar and dark green tie remain without decorations. The rounded beard/chin meets a short broad fitted collar without a stalk or pinching. The complete dark frame and opaque dark charcoal/blue-grey backplate remain, and a dark right-edge note tab is now present. Full white/cyan comparisons show no visible interior holes, lost backing or working-matte ring; the prohibited dot substitution remains the separate visible rejection reason.
entries.visible_limitations: Individual beard hairs, fine spectacle rims and note lettering are not readable at 65x67 and are not rejection grounds. The source marks are visibly irregular gray groups while the native return clearly uses repeated round dots; the rejection depends on that visible shape substitution, not on reading glyphs or numeric alpha values.
